messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a big spike of preemptive evictions in ephemeral GPU pools in us-west-2 over the past 6h. Latency SLOs for several customers spiked when fallback routing kicked in. 

mica: Ugh. Any correlation with spot reclaim events or just noisy tenants?

alex: Mostly reclaim + a couple of tenants sending very bursty batched infer requests. Evictions show up as a mix: graceful preempts and forced OOMs. PromQL I ran: `sum(inference_evictions_total{pool="ephemeral-usw2"}) by (reason)` shows reclaim ~= 60%, oom ~= 25%, other ~= 15%.

sanjay: Do we have per-tenant burst credits configured for ephemeral pools? We built a naive token-bucket early this year but I thought it was disabled for cost-savings.

alex: Token-bucket exists but it's global per-pool and not aware of preemptible lifetime or KV cache pressure. So it doesn't protect against tenants that send very large short-lived batches.

kai: Related: network egress from those hosts also hit a soft quota earlier which aggravated retries. Some tenants re-tried aggressively and amplified the problem. We saw queue depth climb on the PDE side.

mica: OK. Proposed short-term: 1) enable per-tenant soft rate-limiter on ephemeral pools (low friction) 2) add a short eviction backoff window (e.g., mark tenant as low-priority for N minutes after an eviction) 3) route affected requests to a smaller quantized model as fallback. Thoughts?

sanjay: +1 to backoff window. We should be careful with backoff length: too long penalizes noisy-but-legit tenants; too short doesn't help. Maybe make it adaptive: exponential backoff on repeated evictions within a 1h window.

kai: For fallback routing, can we ensure consistency? Some product teams will hate quality regressions. Maybe only fallback for non-SLO-critical routes or when latency spikes > 200ms.

alex: Agree. We can tie fallbacks to route metadata (route.slo_critical = true/false). For critical routes, instead fall back to dedicated if available, otherwise queue briefly + shed non-essential tokens.

mica: Medium-term idea: predictive preemption model that uses historical reclaim windows + tenant burstiness to proactively drain VMs before reclaim windows begin. That reduces forced OOMs and KV cache churn. Would require improving our reclaim signal ingestion and a small ML model.

sanjay: That sounds promising but non-trivial. Also need to update billing/costing because draining early wastes preemptible time. Trade-off analysis needed.

kai: Also we should instrument a new metric: `tenant_eviction_impact{tenant,region}` scoring combined latency delta * request_volume so ops can prioritize. Right now evictions are just a count so we don't know business impact.

ops-bot: Incident note: automated route failover executed at 2025-08-12T03:14:30Z for ephemeral-usw2, affected routes: 5, rollback: none.

alex: Action items I can take: - enable per-tenant soft rate-limiter (config only) for ephemeral-usw2 - add eviction backoff flag to router (start with 2min fixed) - create dashboard for `tenant_eviction_impact`. Will open PRs and a runbook update.

mica: I'll scope the predictive draining RFC and cost tradeoffs; will sync with product on fallback policies.

sanjay: I'll prototype an adaptive token-bucket algorithm and a unit test harness to simulate tenants with different burst profiles.

kai: I'll add the `tenant_eviction_impact` metric to our telemetry schema and wire it into the alerts. Also will add a small dashboard tile to Console for per-route impact.

alex: Cool. Can we get a quick rollback plan if the soft rate-limiter causes false positives? We should be able to toggle by tag.

mica: Yes, flag rollout via config service and a canary targeting 10% of hosts, with a fast kill switch.

sanjay: ETA on initial config rollout?

alex: I can do config change + dashboard today and start the 10% canary tomorrow morning. Will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

kai: Thanks. After canary we should run a 6h blast to see evictions and latencies. Add the canary to the incident playbook as well. :eyes:
